title: Foundational Alphabet Assessment
description: Test your mastery of foundational sounds in Tamil and English

questions.text: Which Tamil vowel sounds like 'a' in 'father'?

options.feedback: Correct! அ is an open vowel sound similar to 'a' in father.
இ sounds like 'i' in sit, not 'a' in father.
உ sounds like 'u' in book, not 'a' in father.

questions.text: Which Tamil consonant has the SAME sound as English M?

options.feedback: Perfect! ம and M are both bilabial nasal sounds - they're identical!
ப sounds like P, not M.
க is a velar sound, different from M.

questions.text: How many foundational Tamil sounds (vowels + consonants) should you master FIRST?

options.feedback: That's the total alphabet! Start with the foundational set first.
Excellent! The foundational set has 3 simple vowels and 8 core consonants.
Too few! The foundational set includes 11 sounds.

questions.text: How many foundational English sounds (vowels + consonants) should you master FIRST?

options.feedback: That's all the letters! Start with core sounds first.
Correct! English foundational set has 5 short vowels and 8 common consonants.
Close, but it's 13 foundational sounds in English.

questions.text: Which English sound has NO Tamil equivalent at the foundational level?

options.feedback: M has a parallel in Tamil: ம (ma).
Right! S is a fricative sound. Tamil has no fricative sounds at foundational level.
L has a parallel in Tamil: ல (la).

questions.text: Which pair of letters represent PARALLEL sounds in Tamil and English?

options.feedback: Excellent! Both are identical bilabial stop sounds.
These are very different sounds with no parallel.
These are unique sounds to each language at foundational level.

questions.text: In the word 'அம்மா' (mother), which foundational sounds are used?

options.feedback: Perfect! அம்மா uses the foundational vowel அ and consonant ம.
These sounds are not in அம்மா (ammā).
These sounds are not in அம்மா (ammā).

questions.text: Which articulation feature do Tamil த (tha), English T, and Tamil ந (na), English N share?

options.feedback: Great understanding! All these sounds use the alveolar ridge (behind teeth).
Labial sounds use the lips, like P/ப and M/ம.
They do share features - they're all alveolar sounds.

questions.text: What is the teaching strategy for sounds that are PARALLEL in both languages?

options.text: Learn them separately with no comparison
options.feedback: Actually, comparing parallel sounds helps learners see connections!

options.text: Start with parallel sounds to build confidence and see connections
options.feedback: Exactly! Parallel sounds (like M/ம, P/ப, T/த) build confidence through recognition.

options.text: Skip them and focus only on unique sounds
options.feedback: Parallel sounds are important bridges between the languages!

questions.text: Which vowel pair shows Tamil and English sounds that are DIFFERENT?

options.text: Tamil இ (i) and English I - both are front vowels
options.feedback: These are actually parallel sounds, both front vowels!

options.text: English E /ɛ/ - Tamil has no equivalent at foundational level
options.feedback: Correct! English E (as in 'bed') is a mid-front vowel unique to English.

options.text: Tamil அ (a) and English A - both are open vowels
options.feedback: These are parallel sounds, both open vowels!

tamil.identify: Can identify 11 Tamil sounds when heard
tamil.produce: Can produce sounds with reasonable approximation
tamil.match: Can match Tamil script to sound
tamil.apply: Can use sounds in 2-3 simple family words

english.identify: Can identify 13 English sounds when heard
english.produce: Can produce sounds with reasonable approximation
english.match: Can match English letters to sounds
english.apply: Can use sounds in 2-3 simple CVC words

crossLinguistic.recognize_same: Recognizes parallel sounds (M, P, N, L, R, T)
crossLinguistic.recognize_unique: Recognizes unique sounds (S, B, O, E in English; க, ய in Tamil)
crossLinguistic.transfer: Can transfer pronunciation knowledge between languages
